desc: Derive formal model: per cell, state = set of edges with endpoints; list the 4 A-states and 2 B-states; express the torus matching as equality constraints on shared edges, defining binary variables h[i][j] and v[i][j].
Prove the propagation structure: A-cell ⇔ a≠c,b≠d; B-cell ⇔ a=c,b=d,a≠b; requires even A-parity per row and column.
Reduce to counting: free vars x_j=v(0,j), y_i=h(i,0); each B-cell gives x_j⊕y_i = 1⊕V(i,j)⊕H(i,j); count = 2^{components} via weighted DSU, or 0 if inconsistent/parity fails.
Write a brute-force enumerator (itertools.product over per-cell states) for tiny grids to validate the reduction, including sample 3 and random small grids.
Implement the main solution: parse input, per case compute A-grid, row/col parity check, prefix XORs V and H, weighted DSU over H+W nodes, process B-cells, output 0 or 2^components mod 998244353.
Cross-check brute force vs. fast solution on samples (2,0,2 all match), 300 random 2×2–3×3 grids, and 60 random 2×4/4×2 grids — all agree.
Verify prefix XOR indexing, DSU parity correctness, fast input parsing, and small H/W wrap-around cases (covered by 2×2/2×3/2×4 random tests).
